newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian dollar deposits quietly steady in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Asian dollar deposits quietly steady in late trade.

text.p: Asian dollar deposit rates were quietly steady in moderate trade with most traders sidelined ahead of tonight's release of the U.S. weekly jobless claims, April international trade and Philadelphia Federal Reserve's June survey data, dealers said on Thursday.
Weekly jobless claims for the week ended June 14, are forecast to be around 333,000 compared with 339,000 reported in the previous week.
The April U.S. trade gap is expected to widen to US$10.0 billion against March's US$8.51 billion.
June's Philadelphia Fed survey is expected to show a reading of 7.3 from a reading of 1.6 in May.

"Rates were steady to easier in the morning on some position adjustments. Some people are waiting for fresh clues to market direction from tonight's release of the weekly jobless claims, international trade and Philadelphia Fed survey figures," a local dealer said.
"But unless the numbers are way off market expectations, I don't think there will be much impact here," he said.
In day-to-day rates, Thursday/Friday and weekend eased 1/16 percentage point each to a common 5-9/16 5-7/16 percent.
Week-fixed was unchanged from Wednesday's 5-5/8 5-1/2 percent.
Among longer dates, two-months was unchanged at 5-11/16 5-9/16 percent, four-months unchangd at 5-3/4 5-5/8, six-months unchanged at 5-7/8 5-3/4 and twelve-months unchanged at 6-1/16 5-15/16 percent.
